claim: CoGo New Project flow: choose template, app name, location, language, minimum SDK, optional Kotlin DSL, then create and wait for Project initialized.
procedure: Set App name and verify package name

claim: The App name is human-facing; package/application ID is an identity. CoGo automatically updates the package field based on app name, but the developer should review it.
No Activity is a blank template requiring the developer to create executable code and Activity setup manually.
procedure: Use only when full manual control is intended

claim: Empty Activity creates a simple MainActivity with no navigation or interaction elements according to CoGo help.
procedure: Choose for a small conventional starter app
Inspect generated UI files before editing

claim: Basic Activity scaffolds a MainActivity with a floating action button.
procedure: Use if the FAB starter is relevant

claim: Navigation Drawer Activity scaffolds a side navigation drawer and FAB; Bottom Navigation Activity provides three bottom navigation sections.
procedure: Choose navigation scaffold only when the app information architecture fits

claim: Legacy Activity (No AndroidX) uses outdated Android Support Library and is recommended only when an explicit legacy compatibility need exists.
procedure: Prefer AndroidX-based template for new projects
warning: Do not select merely because an old tutorial uses it.

claim: Compose Activity is a Kotlin-only template for building UI in Kotlin rather than separate XML layout files.
procedure: Select Compose template for Kotlin Compose projects

claim: Minimum SDK is the oldest Android version the app intends to support; it is distinct from targetSdk and compileSdk.
procedure: Use offered template value unless support policy requires change

claim: The Gradle DSL choice is independent from the source language; follow the project’s actual build.gradle vs build.gradle.kts files.
procedure: Use matching Groovy or Kotlin DSL syntax

claim: Java/Kotlin source belongs in the app source set and package path; XML layouts belong under app/src/main/res/layout.
procedure: Use resource directories for UI resources

claim: CoGo Sync project saves unsaved changes, refreshes the IDE project model from Gradle structure/libraries/settings, and reports information in Build Output.
procedure: Sync after dependency or Gradle settings changes

claim: CoGo lets users browse/search/select one or more Gradle tasks through the Run tasks panel and see results in Build Output.
CoGo help documents APK outputs under CodeOnTheGoProjects/AppName/app/build/outputs/apk/debug or release.
procedure: Use Build Output/project files to confirm exact artifact path and name

claim: CoGo supports XML/View System and Jetpack Compose; official help identifies Compose as Kotlin-only.
procedure: Use XML/View for Java or conventional XML projects
Use Compose template for Kotlin-first Compose UI

claim: CoGo help documents android.buildFeatures.compose=true for Kotlin DSL and compose true for Groovy DSL, but complete Compose compiler/dependency configuration depends on project toolchain.
procedure: Do not add only the feature flag to an arbitrary old project and assume complete setup
warning: The syntax snippet is not a complete compatibility recipe.

claim: CoGo 26.38 introduced updated stack values Kotlin 2.3.21, AGP 9.3.1, Gradle 9.6.1, Build Tools 36.0.0.
procedure: Use current generated templates for new projects

claim: Projects made on CoGo 26.37 or earlier may fail after updating to 26.38+; new templates on the new stack should need no manual migration.
procedure: If it fails, identify whether libs.versions.toml exists
Follow official migration case A or B

claim: The official migration guide distinguishes projects with and without gradle/libs.versions.toml and gives different edit steps.
In the new AGP 9.3.1 stack, an error saying the Kotlin Android plugin is no longer required can indicate an obsolete Kotlin plugin line remains.
procedure: Apply official migration instructions only when applicable

claim: CoGo is offline-capable, but uncached external dependencies/plugins may need network access.
procedure: Check exact dependency and offline flag
Only disable --offline when network access is available/allowed

claim: Quick Build is experimental; needs feature flag and restart, a launchable Activity, single-process app, debug variant, and extra memory/storage.
procedure: Create proxy app with first Quick Build
Use normal build for final verification

claim: Quick Build does not support library/plugin projects or apps that start extra processes.
procedure: Use normal Build/Quick Run for these project types

claim: Diagnose from the first meaningful error in Build Output, not only the final BUILD FAILED summary.
procedure: Check the relevant file and line
Change one cause at a time

claim: A long error mentioning InternalProblems after the CoGo toolchain upgrade can indicate the AGP version is still old; the migration guide advises setting it to 9.3.1 in the relevant migration case.
The new-stack migration guide says an error about kotlinOptions being an error requires updating the old Kotlin target configuration as documented.
procedure: Replace legacy target block only when migration case applies

claim: An Android app making network requests generally needs INTERNET permission in the manifest; additional permissions depend on actual behavior.
procedure: Do not embed privileged API secrets

claim: Add one dependency at a time and verify coordinate, version, minSdk, toolchain compatibility, license, and offline cache availability.
procedure: Edit module dependency and catalog coherently

claim: Manifest components/permissions should be added only when required and should be checked against existing declarations and merged library manifests.
CoGo help recommends a unique keystore for an app intended for distribution rather than relying on the default installer-provided key.
CoGo help describes selecting Release in Build variants and building after signing configuration is set.
Build success means configured variant compiled/packaged, not that app features work correctly.
CoGo release 26.39 notes clickable build errors/warnings in logs, which can navigate to the relevant line.
Do not assume ViewBinding, package path, activity name, or generated layout name; inspect template files first.
procedure: Read generated Activity and module build file
Make a file plan from observed structure

claim: CoGo Build help documents building, then installing and launching the app from the UI.
CoGo terminal can run shell commands and local Git; official help shows git init for local version control.
Version catalogs centralize dependency versions in gradle/libs.versions.toml but are optional in the updated stack.
procedure: Avoid adding catalog merely to make a new stack build

claim: Wait for the CoGo Project initialized message before assuming setup completed.
Legacy No AndroidX template is intended only for explicit compatibility with old Android Support Library.
Logs and build files may contain tokens, passwords, private URLs, or signing secrets; redact before sharing.
A good CoGo coding answer gives exact project assumptions, file paths, complete file contents, UI steps, build instructions, acceptance checks, and troubleshooting.
procedure: Use one code block per file

claim: Run only the narrowest Gradle task that answers the next diagnostic question; task availability can vary by module/variant.
Confirm exact APK filename/path from Build Output or project files; do not infer artifact names from generic templates.
A library minSdk requirement can conflict with the app support range; resolve the policy tradeoff deliberately.
procedure: Explain devices excluded if minSdk increases

claim: Use standard Build/Quick Run for final verification even if Quick Build is used during rapid iteration.
procedure: Test actual APK and release variant separately

claim: Before toolchain migration, create a backup or version-control commit so the project can be restored.
CoGo help describes a Compose preview action in the command slider for previewing layout without building the app.
procedure: Use preview for fast layout iteration

claim: For CoGo support/debug reports, include device model, Android version, CoGo version, logs, screenshots, and reproducible steps when available.
procedure: Include the exact action and first error

claim: The official CoGo weight converter tutorial uses Empty Activity, app name WeightConverter, Java, and API 21 as the tutorial example.
procedure: Set exact app name if using tutorial files
Choose minSdk based on actual support needs; API 21 is only the tutorial example
warning: Do not treat tutorial API 21 as a universal recommendation.

claim: The official tutorial edits MainActivity.java under app/src/main/java/com/example/weightconverter and activity_main.xml under app/src/main/res/layout.
procedure: Edit Activity and XML layout at their actual paths

claim: The weight converter UI consists of an EditText for decimal quantity, a Spinner for kg/lbs, and a TextView for converted measurement.
Both input text changes and unit dropdown selection should update conversion result through one shared updateConversionResult method.
Numeric input can be empty or partially typed; conversion logic should handle this without crashing.
A successful weight converter test includes known conversions in both directions and live updates when quantity/unit changes.
procedure: Test empty input and live changes

claim: CoGo Help explains that long-pressing interface elements or selected code and tapping Help can reveal tooltips and deeper documentation.
procedure: Long-press UI item or selected code

claim: For a new project, build the untouched generated template before implementing features when practical to isolate setup/toolchain errors from code errors.
